newsitem.title: USA: Porsche AG still exploring sport/utility.
newsitem.headline: Porsche AG still exploring sport/utility.

text.p: German sportscar maker Porsche AG is continuing to explore the possibility of offering a sport/utility vehicle, despite the collapse of previous plans to collaborate with Mercedes-Benz on such a vechicle.
Fred Schwab, Porsche Cars North America Inc president, said Thursday a sport/utlity vehicle "is a concept that we continue to be interested in."

Speaking to reporters at the Chicago Auto Show, Schwab declined to say whether Porsche was discussing any specific arrangements with other auto makers, but added "this is not a business where you can sit and let something come to you."

Mercedes-Benz, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, said in January that it had dropped plans to develop a Porsche high-performance sport/utility vehicle based on Mercede's new M-Class sport/utility vehicle, which is being built in the United States.
Schwab said Mercedes told Porcshe it pulled out of the project because it did not believe the vehicle would be profitable enough.
The decision ended two years of effort by the two automakers on the project. "We danced and hugged and kissed with a partner, and it didn't work out," Schwab said.
Schwab also said he expects strong demand for the new Boxster roadster to push Porsche's U.S. sales for 1997 to over 14,000 units, doubling the 7,144 cars Porsche sold here in 1996.

In January, Porsche said its U.S. sales more than doubled to 1,278 cars. Schwab said dealer orders have been taken for nearly all of the Boxster's allocated for the U.S. market in the 1997 model year.

He added that a decision by Porsche to build about 5,000 Boxsters annually at a Finnish plant owned by Valmet OY will allow Porsche to expand worldwide production for the fiscal 1997 year ending July 31 to about 35,000 cars from about 20,000 cars in fiscal 1996.
